evidence.quote: I would be supporting "good news" rate cuts later this year.
I support looking through any tariff effects on near term-inflation when setting the policy rate.
So I do not believe one can use 2021 and 2022 as a basis for predicting what will happen to the persistence of inflation arising from tariffs.
As of today, I see downside risks to economic activity and employment and upside risks to inflation in the second half of 2025
Fortunately, the strong labor market and progress on inflation through April gives me additional time to see how trade negotiations play out and the economy evolves.
I do expect tariffs will result in an increase in the unemployment rate that will, all else equal, probably linger.

parsed.rationale: The speaker argues tariff inflation will be transitory with anchored expectations, advocates looking through it, and signals conditional rate cuts later this year. Labor market is described as solid now but expected to weaken, tilting the balance dovish.
